etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Medieval Latin schēma (“figure, form”), from Ancient Greek σχῆμα (skhêma, “form, shape”), from ἔχω (ékhō, “I hold”). Doublet of schema. Compare sketch.

definitions.definition: (rhetoric, obsolete) An artful deviation from the ordinary arrangement of words. [16th–17th c.]
(astrology) A representation of the aspects of the celestial bodies for any moment or at a given event. [from 17th c.]

quote.citation: 1815 February 24, [Walter Scott], Guy Mannering; or, The Astrologer. […], volume (please specify |volume=I to III), Edinburgh:  […]  James Ballantyne and Co. for Longman, Hurst, Rees, Orme, and Brown, […]; and Archibald Constable and Co., […], →OCLC:
quote.text: a blue case, from which was drawn a scheme of nativity

definitions.definition: A systematic plan of future action. [from 18th c.]

quote.citation: c. 1713, Jonathan Swift, Thoughts on Various Subjects:
quote.text: The stoical scheme of supplying our wants by lopping off our desires, is like cutting off our feet when we want shoes.

quote.citation: 2013 June 1, “Ideas coming down the track”, in The Economist‎[1], volume 407, number 8838, page 13 (Technology Quarterly):
quote.text: A “moving platform” scheme […] is more technologically ambitious than maglev trains even though it relies on conventional rails. Local trains would use side-by-side rails to roll alongside intercity trains and allow passengers to switch trains by stepping through docking bays. This set-up solves several problems […].

definitions.definition: A plot or secret, devious plan.
An orderly combination of related parts.

quote.citation: 1689 (indicated as 1690), [John Locke], An Essay Concerning Humane Understanding. […], London:  […]  Eliz[abeth] Holt, for Thomas Basset, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: the appearance and outward scheme of things

quote.citation: 1706, Francis Atterbury, A Sermon Preach'd in the Cathedral Church of St. Paul; at the Funeral of My. Tho. Bennett:
quote.text: such a scheme of things as shall at once take in time and eternity

quote.citation: 1754, Jonathan Edwards, The Freedom of the Will:
quote.text: arguments  […]  sufficient to support and demonstrate a whole scheme of moral philosophy

quote.citation: 1849–1861, Thomas Babington Macaulay, chapter XX, in The History of England from the Accession of James the Second, volume (please specify |volume=I to V), London: Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, →OCLC:
quote.text: The Revolution came and changed his whole scheme of life.

definitions.definition: A chart or diagram of a system or object.

quote.citation: April 29, 1694, Robert South, A Sermon Preached at Westminster Abbey
quote.text: to draw an exact scheme of Constantinople, or a map of France

definitions.definition: (mathematics) A mathematical structure that generalizes the notion of an algebraic variety in several ways, such as taking account of multiplicities and allowing "varieties" defined over any commutative ring. Formally, a locally ringed space that admits a covering by open sets, each of which is isomorphic to an affine scheme (i.e. the spectrum of some commutative ring).
(UK, chiefly Scotland, colloquial) A council housing estate. [from 20th c.]

quote.citation: 2008, James Kelman, Kieron Smith, Boy, Penguin, published 2009, page 101:
quote.text: It was all too dear. They all just put their prices up because it was out in the scheme.

quote.citation: 2023 July 2, David Barnett, quoting Irvine Welsh, “‘Choose drugs?’ 30 years after he wrote Trainspotting, Irvine Welsh says life is tougher now”, in The Observer‎[2], →ISSN:
quote.text: “You can’t really say to the kids in the schemes [Scottish council estates][sic]: don’t do drugs, they’ll wreck your life, you’ll never get a job or a house or buy nice things.”

definitions.definition: (Internet) Part of a uniform resource identifier indicating the protocol or other purpose, such as http: or news:.
(UK, pensions) A portfolio of pension plans with related benefits comprising multiple independent members.
(intransitive) To plot, or contrive a plan; to manuever.

quote.citation: 1987 November 8, Ron Hansen, “CHILDREN'S BOOKS; DISCOVERING THE OPPOSITE SEX”, in The New York Times‎[3]:
quote.text: Laura snatches coins from inside a truck to make a telephone call, scrounges shoes and clothes for them at a municipal beach, schemes to get a room key so she and Howie can sleep overnight in the Starlight Motel, steals a Jeepster from a deputy sheriff who's trying to arrest them.

quote.citation: 2012 April 26, Tasha Robinson, “Film: Reviews: The Pirates! Band Of Misfits”, in The Onion AV Club‎[4]:
quote.text: The openly ridiculous plot has The Pirate Captain (Hugh Grant) scheming to win the Pirate Of The Year competition, even though he’s a terrible pirate, far outclassed by rivals voiced by Jeremy Piven and Salma Hayek.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To plan; to contrive; to manuever.

quote.text: He schemed a plot. He made use of the hotel's stationery to write a letter.
